paragraphs: The 650i has been a mainstay of the 6 Series diesel range since 2012, spanning two generations under one badge. Early F06/F12/F13 models from 2012 to 2015 use the N47, a 2.0-litre diesel that's part of a family known for a specific timing chain issue. From late 2015 onwards, across both the F06/F12/F13 and later the F06/F12/F13, the 650i switched to the B47, a newer, significantly more reliable unit that doesn't share the N47's timing chain concerns. Knowing which one your car has matters, because the components and the known wear pattern differ - which is exactly why we confirm your exact engine by registration before quoting.
about.boldParagraph: The 650i is no longer in production, but we continue to rebuild and replace engines for every one still on the road.

cards.body: A 4.4‑litre V8 twin‑turbo petrol engine fitted to the 650i from launch in 2011 through to the 2015 model‑year update. This is BMW's original hot‑vee V8 design, with the turbochargers nestled in the V of the engine — a layout that generates significant heat and is known to cause accelerated wear on valve seals and coolant components over time. We replace timing chains, valve seals, coolant components and bearings as standard on every N63 rebuild.

The technical‑update version of the N63, introduced for the 2015 model year and fitted to the 650i until production ended in 2018. It shares the same 4.4‑litre V8 twin‑turbo layout but includes revised pistons, timing chain guides, and cooling system upgrades — a meaningful improvement, but still subject to the same hot‑vee turbo heat‑soak pattern as its predecessor. We service it to the same standard as the N63, with the same component replacements on every rebuild.

compatibility.intro: Because the 650i spans two engine revisions (N63 and N63TU) within the same chassis generations, a like‑for‑like replacement requires correct identification — you cannot simply swap an early N63 into a later TU‑spec car without accounting for ECU and ancillary differences. Before we quote or supply anything, we confirm:

points.text: Your exact engine code (N63 or N63TU) via registration or VIN
Any electronics or ECU considerations specific to your build

compatibility.footer: This is why we always start with your registration rather than a generic 650i quote — it protects you from paying for parts that don't fit your actual car.
